diagnostic_evidence.quote: in a Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset \R^2$, where $p \geq 2$ is an integer, and $q\in C^{s}(\Omega \times [0, T])$ for a given $s > 1$.
Here and throughout, $H^{s}$ denotes the standard $L^2$-based Sobolev space.

issues.failure_explanation: Lipschitz boundary normals can jump, so even smooth solutions need not have H^s normal traces. For example, take a domain with one right-angle corner and smooth boundary elsewhere, q=0, and a smooth incoming plane wave in direction (1,-1)/sqrt(2). Its Dirichlet trace is smooth in arclength through the corner, whereas its two normal traces have opposite nonzero values. That jump is not in H^s for s>1. The wave can vanish initially, so compatibility does not fix this defect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the Lipschitz-domain theory using weak conormal traces and dual boundary pairings, and supply the corresponding energy-space small-data differentiability argument instead of asserting an H^s normal trace.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed H^s-valued measurement operator is unsupported in the stated Lipschitz-domain setting, including polygonal geometries.
issues.title: The asserted high-order DN regularity fails on Lipschitz domains
issues.why_classification: A contained change of functional framework and a trace/linearization argument are needed, but the existing inverse construction can be retained.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\varphi_h \in C^{\infty}_c(\mathbb{R})$ is a cutoff function supported on $[-h, h]$ with $\varphi_h(0) = 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: Smoothness of the cutoff does not imply smoothness of its cube root or square root. An allowed nonnegative cutoff with an interior quadratic zero gives a cube root behaving like |l-a|^(2/3) and a square root behaving like |l-a|. These fail the required H^{s+1} regularity for s>=1 on a transverse boundary patch. Without nonnegativity, the pointwise method's square root can also fail to be real.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the cutoff explicitly as phi_h=rho_h^6 with rho_h a nonnegative smooth compactly supported function satisfying rho_h(0)=1.
issues.overall_effect: Both reconstruction procedures can prescribe boundary directions outside the class required for higher-order linearization.
issues.title: The cutoff assumptions do not make the fractional-root boundary waves admissible
issues.why_classification: This local cutoff choice makes both fractional roots smooth without changing the wave geometry, concentration limit, or recovery guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This can then be repeated for all parameter tuples in the admissible set $W_{\text{Radon}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The spatial zero extension of the stated q need not be Lipschitz, and the claimed all-tuples convergence can actually fail. Take Omega=(-1,1)^2, q=1, theta=e_1, eta=1, and an admissible interior time. The line has empty intersection with the open domain, so its stated Radon integral is zero. The normalized Gaussian volume integral instead tends to 1, receiving half the mass across the flat boundary. If the boundary line is included, its line integral is 2, still not 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the all-tuples assertion by an approximate-identity result at Lebesgue points of the Radon data of the zero extension, and prove that version. Almost-everywhere Radon recovery still suffices for inversion. Retaining the all-tuples formula would instead require an appropriate continuous or Lipschitz zero-extension assumption.
issues.overall_effect: The formula does not recover the Radon transform at every advertised tuple for the stated potential and domain classes.
issues.title: The Radon recovery formula applies a compact-support lemma to an inadmissible zero extension
issues.why_classification: A contained approximate-identity argument and a limited weakening of pointwise scope suffice; the main Radon inversion approach need not be replaced.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now, when $\tau$ is large, the product $v_0 v_1 v_2^2 \approx \tau^{\frac{3}{2}} \e^{-\tau (|x-x_0|^2 + (t-t_0)^2)}$ near the point $(x_0, t_0)$

issues.failure_explanation: Writing a=theta·(x-x_0), b=theta-perp·(x-x_0), and z=t-t_0, the actual Gaussian exponent is -tau[a^2+z^2+(z-b)^2/2], not -tau(a^2+b^2+z^2). The displayed right-hand side consequently tends to 3! sqrt(2) pi^(3/2) q, giving a multiplicative reconstruction error.

issues.failure_explanation: General Dirichlet data are defined only on Sigma, so their ghost-point values are unspecified. Even using the known incident-wave extension does not fix consistency: for the scattered field w=u-f, this prescription sets both boundary and ghost values to zero. If w(x)=a x+O(x^2) near a boundary, substituting that ghost value into the first interior five-point stencil produces a leading error -a/(12h), rather than a consistent second derivative. This persists for smooth solutions and is independent of the interior regularity issue.
